title: Linear lower bounds for generalized orthogonality dimension of Kneser graphs
work: The (Generalized) Orthogonality Dimension of (Generalized) Kneser Graphs: Bounds and Applications
difficulty_reason: The lower bound requires an induction that replaces an orthogonal subspace representation by projected subspaces while preserving every disjoint-set orthogonality relation. When no suitable projection vertex exists, the authors construct nonzero vectors from a chain of subspace intersections and bound their nonorthogonality neighborhoods before extracting a large orthogonal family; this good/bad-vertex dichotomy is a substantive research-level obligation beyond routine qualification-exam dimension calculations.
required_context: Full original article retained, including definitions of generalized orthogonality dimension/Kneser graphs and the ordinary generic-subspace avoidance fact precisely cited to Babai–Frankl3.1.4. Complete source-local good-vertex projection and bad-vertex common-intersection/greedy family proof is945–1018. No hardness corollary or s=2 restatement is counted.
